rootCause: src/geometry/shape.ts declares the discriminated union `Shape`, whose tag was renamed from `kind` to `type` across all three members. Three consumers still narrow on `kind`: src/geometry/area.ts, src/render/label.ts and src/render/legend.ts. In area.ts the failed narrowing cascades a second time — the branch never narrows, so reading `.radius` and `.side` fails too.
expectedFix: Read `type` instead of `kind` at the three consumers, or rename the tag back in src/geometry/shape.ts. One decision at the union declaration settles all eight diagnostics.
purpose: Two things no other fixture covers. First, a cause that is a TYPE ALIAS OF A UNION rather than an interface or a module — the corpus showed that 2339 on a union can resolve to the type-literal (result.ts:12:4) while 2353 on the same type resolves to the alias (result.ts:11:1), which is the sub-grouping asymmetry PROJECT.md §5.1 accepts; here all eight resolve to the alias and fold completely, so the two behaviours are both committed and comparable. Second, it is the only fixture where one root cause produces a SECOND ORDER of diagnostics: the failed narrowing on `kind` leaves the value un-narrowed, so `.radius` and `.side` fail as a consequence of a consequence. Both orders fold onto the same declaration, which is the behaviour to watch if the causality threshold is ever loosened.
